title: Personalized Dose Finding

This tutorial uses orthoDr 2.0.0. See [Get Started](get-started.html) for
installation and the complete R script.

```{r load-package, eval=FALSE}
library(orthoDr)
```

```{r guide, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
source(rprojroot::find_package_root_file("tools", "pkgdown-guide.R"), local = TRUE)
cat(guide_section("Learn a personalized dose and predict"), sep = "\n")
```

## Next steps

Both dose methods use pSAVE as the default starting basis. Supply a
full-column-rank `B.initial` matrix with one row per predictor and `ndr`
columns to use another starting point, including a random one. The function
orthonormalizes the supplied basis before fitting. pSAVE is one initialization
option; final dose accuracy can vary with the starting point.
Use unit-length starting columns or an orthonormal basis. Extremely small
columns can be rejected as numerically rank deficient.

The finite-sample dose kernel uses the individual projected coordinates.
Rotating a basis or rescaling predictors can therefore change a fitted rule.
Apply any chosen predictor preprocessing consistently to training and new data.

See `orthoDr_pdose()` for candidate grids, bandwidths, initialization, and
regularization, and the numerical stopping criteria. The
[method paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/asaa087) explains the distinction
between direct and pseudo-direct learning and their assumptions.
